structuralStrata.description: 5 high-impact 50-question mastery bundles covering Government definition, institutions, the state, and governance.

bundles.name: Bundle 1 — Definition of Government (As Institution of the State)

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state may be defined as:
options: A body of people who make and enforce laws for a particular society.
A machinery established by the state to organise, manage the affairs of the state and administer its functions and duties.
The process of carrying out the day-to-day administration of a country.
The study of agencies, political institutions and the dynamics of the state.
questions.answer: A machinery established by the state to organise, manage the affairs of the state and administer its functions and duties.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state is the machinery established by the state to organise, manage the affairs of the state and administer its functions and duties.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes government as an instrument of the state?
options: It is a voluntary association of people with common interests.
It is the means through which the will of the state is formulated, expressed, and realized.
It is an academic discipline studied in universities.
It is a temporary body that changes with every election.
questions.answer: It is the means through which the will of the state is formulated, expressed, and realized.
questions.explanation: Government is the means through which the will of the state is formulated, expressed, and realized. It is endowed with power and authority to provide the basic needs of the people.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state is endowed with power and authority for which primary purpose?
options: To recruit and train political leaders.
To provide the basic needs of the people, including social welfare and security.
To conduct elections for the state.
To settle disputes between political parties only.
questions.answer: To provide the basic needs of the people, including social welfare and security.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state is endowed with power and authority to provide the basic needs of the people which include social welfare and security.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three major arms of government as an institution of the state?
questions.explanation: The three major arms of government are the Executive, the Legislature, and the Judiciary. The Civil Service is not one of the three arms.

questions.text: The arm of government concerned with policy formulation and implementation is the:
questions.explanation: The Executive arm of government is concerned with policy formulation and implementation.

questions.text: The arm of government concerned with law making which every member of society must obey is the:
questions.explanation: The Legislature is concerned with law making which every member of the society must obey.

questions.text: The arm of government that concentrates mainly on the interpretation of the law and decides how to apply laws in specific disputes is the:
questions.explanation: The Judiciary arm of government concentrates mainly on the interpretation of the law and decides how to apply the laws in specific disputes.

questions.text: A body of people and institutions that make and enforce laws for a particular society is called:
questions.explanation: Government is the group of people to whom legitimate authorities are conferred to govern a country or a state. They make laws, implement and formulate policies, interpret laws and settle disputes in society.

questions.text: Government is the machinery established to manage the affairs of the:
questions.explanation: Government is a machinery of the state established to manage the affairs of the people to make society a better place.

questions.text: Government as an institution of a state can be defined as a body that:
options: Settles disputes and interprets law for the state.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state needs to elect few individuals into political offices and empowers them to make laws, guide, control and regulate the laws. The three organs or arms of government are very essential in this aspect.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state means the:
options: Method of organizing political parties and pressure groups.
Process of decision making in a society.
Method of resolution of conflicts among people.
Structures and systems for decision making in a society.
questions.answer: Structures and systems for decision making in a society.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state refers to the structures and systems for decision making in a society. It is the machinery through which the will of the state is formulated, expressed, and realized.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines government as an institution of a state?
options: An institution established for class struggles.
Machinery established for exercising political parties.
A process of organizing societal values.
The art through which political parties are managed.
questions.answer: Machinery established for exercising political parties.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of a state is the machinery established by the state to organise, manage the affairs of the state and administer its functions and duties.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state refers to the:
options: Judiciary, the president and his ministers.
Legislature, the executive and the judiciary.
questions.answer: Legislature, the executive and the judiciary.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state refers to the legislature that makes law, the executive that formulates policies and implements them, and the judiciary that interprets the law.

questions.text: The institution through which governments discharge responsibilities is known as:
questions.explanation: The institution through which government discharges responsibilities is known as organs of government. The organs of government enhance and coordinate the affairs of the state.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about government as an institution of the state is INCORRECT?
options: It is a machinery established by the state.
It organises and manages the affairs of the state.
It is a voluntary association that citizens can join or leave at will.
It administers the functions and duties of the state.
questions.answer: It is a voluntary association that citizens can join or leave at will.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state is not a voluntary association. Membership of the state is compulsory, and government is the machinery established to manage its affairs.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state is described as an instrument whose purpose is to:
options: Promote the interests of the ruling party only.
Solve human disputes through law and enforce those solutions through superior power.
Recruit civil servants for the state.
questions.answer: Solve human disputes through law and enforce those solutions through superior power.
questions.explanation: Government is an instrument whose purpose is to solve human disputes through law and to enforce those solutions or laws through superior power.

questions.text: The three organs of government are essential because:
options: They compete with each other for power.
The functions of each organ are stipulated in the constitution.
They are all controlled by the executive.
They are elected by the people directly.
questions.answer: The functions of each organ are stipulated in the constitution.
questions.explanation: Government as the institution of the state directs all the activities of the state because the functions of each organ are stipulated in the constitution.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary function of the Executive arm of government?
questions.explanation: The Executive arm of government is concerned with policy formulation and implementation.

questions.text: The primary function of the Legislature is:
questions.explanation: The Legislature is concerned with law making which every member of the society must obey.

questions.text: The primary function of the Judiciary is:
options: Interpretation of laws and settlement of disputes
questions.answer: Interpretation of laws and settlement of disputes
questions.explanation: The Judiciary concentrates mainly on the interpretation of the law and decides how to apply the laws in specific disputes.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state is necessary because it:
options: Is capable of regulating the day-to-day activities of the citizens.
questions.answer: Is capable of regulating the day-to-day activities of the citizens.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state is essential because it is a body capable of regulating the day-to-day activities of the citizens.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of government as an institution of the state?
questions.explanation: Organising trade unions is not a function of government. The functions of government include law making, defence, protection of lives and property, maintenance of law and order, and administration of justice.

questions.text: The government maintains law and order through the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Government makes laws and enforces them through the legislature, police and prison services. Immigration is not primarily a law and order maintenance organ in this context.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state refers to a body that:
options: Settles disputes between political parties only.
questions.explanation: Government as an institution of the state legislates, executes and adjudicates. It makes laws, implements them, and interprets them.

questions.text: A government performs the following functions EXCEPT:
options: Providing all the needs of its citizens.
questions.answer: Providing all the needs of its citizens.
questions.explanation: It is impossible for the government to provide all the needs of its citizens. It provides basic welfare needs, safeguards life and property, and maintains law and order.

questions.text: The defense of a country is a major function of the:
questions.explanation: The defence of a country is a major function of the government of a state. The government establishes and equips standing armed forces to defend the country from external aggression.

questions.text: Which of the following is an acceptable function of government?
questions.explanation: Maintenance of law and order is an acceptable function of government. Subversion, encouraging struggle for power, and promoting civil disobedience are not acceptable functions.

questions.text: The primary function of government in a state is to:
questions.explanation: The primary function of any government is to maintain peace, law and order in society before the government can function properly.

questions.text: Government can be made responsible and accountable to its citizens through the following methods EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Government can be made responsible and accountable through periodic change of government, political education, and public opinion. Demonstration is a form of violence and not a formal process of deliberations.

questions.text: The functions of the state are achieved through:
questions.explanation: The functions of the state are achieved through the organs of government: the executive formulates and implements policies, the legislature makes laws, and the judiciary interprets laws.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an attribute or characteristic of government?
questions.explanation: Voluntary membership is not an attribute of government. Government has political power, legitimate authority, law making, revenue, workforce, protection, periodic change, and welfare services as attributes.

questions.text: The attribute of government that enables it to control the behaviour of citizens through formulated and implemented policies is:
questions.explanation: Political power is the power that enables government to control the behaviour of citizens through formulated and implemented policies for the benefit of all.

questions.text: Any legally constituted government must have legitimate authority arising from:
questions.explanation: Any legally constituted government must have legitimate authority arising from the social acceptance of the people.

questions.text: Government needs enough revenue from the people which is known as:
questions.explanation: Government needs enough revenue from the people which is known as tax. Tax is used for social amenities and basic infrastructure.

questions.text: The feature of government that provides enough protection and security for the people and their property is:
questions.explanation: Protection is the feature of government that provides enough protection and security for the people and their property so that society can be a place to live in peace, order and unity.

questions.text: No government is permanent, especially one based on people's participation (elective government) known as democracy. This attribute is called:
questions.explanation: Periodic change is the attribute of government that ensures no government is permanent, especially elective governments, which have periodic tenure of either five (5) or four (4) years.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of government?
questions.explanation: Encouraging struggle for power is not a function of government. Government encourages peace and unity in society. The struggle for power can lead to riots and demonstrations.

questions.text: The function of government that involves maintaining good relationships with other countries is:
questions.explanation: The external affairs function of government involves maintaining good relationships with other countries through embassies, high commissions, ambassadors, and high commissioners.

questions.text: The function of government that involves the judiciary is:
questions.explanation: The judiciary is responsible for the administration of justice in the state.

questions.text: Which of the following is a source of government revenue?
questions.explanation: Sources of government revenue include tax, surplus of public sector units, fines and penalties, gifts and grants, borrowings, rates, and fees.

questions.text: A tax is best defined as:
options: A compulsory levy imposed by a public authority against which taxpayers cannot claim anything.
A penalty for a legal offence.
A fee for a specific service rendered.
questions.answer: A compulsory levy imposed by a public authority against which taxpayers cannot claim anything.
questions.explanation: A tax is a compulsory levy imposed by a public authority against which taxpayers cannot claim anything. It is not imposed as a penalty for a legal offence.

questions.text: The main purpose of fines and penalties as a source of government revenue is:
options: To raise revenue from the public.
To force people to follow law and order.
questions.answer: To force people to follow law and order.
questions.explanation: The main purpose of fines and penalties is not to raise revenue but to force people to follow law and order.

questions.text: Gifts and grants as a source of government revenue are:
options: Voluntary contributions from private individuals or non-government donors.
questions.answer: Voluntary contributions from private individuals or non-government donors.
questions.explanation: Gifts are voluntary contributions from private individuals or non-government donors to the government fund for specific purposes.

questions.text: Rates as a source of government revenue refer to:
options: Local taxation levied by or for local government.
questions.answer: Local taxation levied by or for local government.
questions.explanation: Rates refer to local taxation, i.e., taxation levied by (or for) local rather than central government. They are proportional to the estimated rentable value of properties.

questions.text: A fee is best described as:
options: A payment to defray the cost of each recurring service undertaken by government.
A penalty for breaking the law.
questions.answer: A payment to defray the cost of each recurring service undertaken by government.
questions.explanation: A fee is a payment to defray the cost of each recurring service undertaken by the government, primarily in the public interest.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a source of government revenue?
questions.explanation: Civil disobedience is not a source of government revenue. Sources include tax, borrowings, fines and penalties, gifts and grants, rates, and fees.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state is different from other human associations because:
options: It has legitimate authority to fine, imprison or execute law breakers.
It cannot use force to ensure obedience.
questions.answer: It has legitimate authority to fine, imprison or execute law breakers.
questions.explanation: The state has legitimate authority to fine, imprison or execute law breakers. Other human associations do not have such authority over their members.

questions.text: The rules made by the state are:
options: Applicable only to members of the ruling party.
Authoritative and generally binding on all residents of the state.
questions.answer: Authoritative and generally binding on all residents of the state.
questions.explanation: Rules made by the state are authoritative and generally binding on all residents of the state, unlike other human associations whose rules are not applicable to non-members.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about government as an institution of the state is TRUE?
options: It is a temporary association that disappears after elections.
It has no power to enforce laws.
questions.explanation: The state is a permanent association. Government may change but the state remains. Other associations are non-permanent and may disappear and re-emerge.

questions.text: Government as an institution of the state is described as the machinery through which:
options: The will of the state is formulated, expressed, and realized.
questions.answer: The will of the state is formulated, expressed, and realized.
questions.explanation: Government is the means through which the will of the state is formulated, expressed, and realized. It is endowed with power and authority to provide the basic needs of the people.

bundles.name: Bundle 2 — Government as an Art of Governing & Academic Field of Study

questions.text: Government as an art of governing or process of administration may be defined as:
options: A machinery established by the state to manage its affairs.
A body vested with the power and authority for maintaining security, peace, and stability by making and enforcing laws.
The study of agencies, political institutions and the dynamics of the state.
A voluntary association of people with common interests.
questions.answer: A body vested with the power and authority for maintaining security, peace, and stability by making and enforcing laws.
questions.explanation: Government as an art of governing or process of administration is a body vested with the power and authority for maintaining security, peace, and stability by making and enforcing conventional and fundamental laws in a given state or society.

questions.text: The process of carrying out the affairs of a country is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Government is seen as an art of governing or process of administration because supreme powers of the state affairs are vested in some few individuals to maintain peace, order and security of the state. The process of carrying out the affairs of a country is referred to as governance.

questions.text: Which of the following is related to government as a process of governing?
options: The role of pressure groups within the state.
Disagreement between state and local government.
questions.explanation: The term government as a process of governing also refers to implementations, making, reviewing and amending laws in society. This administrative structure is known as the process of governing people.

questions.text: Government as the act of governing means the:
options: Activities of pressure groups and political parties.
Activities by which government policies are made and implemented.
questions.answer: Activities by which government policies are made and implemented.
questions.explanation: Government as the act of governing means the activities by which government policies are made and implemented.

questions.text: Government as an art of governance refers to the process of:
questions.explanation: Government as an art of governance refers to the process of making and enforcing laws. It involves the formulation and implementation of policies in the state.

questions.text: Government can be described as the art of:
questions.explanation: Government can be described as the art of making and enforcing laws.

questions.text: In the process of governing, input refers to the:
options: Decisions and actions of the authorities.
Regulations made by the government for individuals and groups.
Demands made by individuals and groups for actions by the authorities.
Demands which have become official policies.
questions.answer: Demands made by individuals and groups for actions by the authorities.
questions.explanation: In the process of governing, input refers to the demands made by individuals and groups for actions by the authorities.

questions.text: In the process of governing, output refers to the:
questions.explanation: In the process of governing, output refers to the decisions of the government.

questions.text: Policy formulation involves developing strategies for dealing with policy issues which have been placed on:
questions.explanation: Policy formulation involves developing strategies for dealing with policy issues which have been placed on an agenda.

questions.text: In policy formulation, effectiveness refers to:
options: Strategies that are acceptable to the people.
Valid, workable strategies that address the situation.
Strategies that are popular with politicians.
Strategies that are cheap to implement.
questions.answer: Valid, workable strategies that address the situation.
questions.explanation: Effectiveness refers to valid, workable strategies that address the situation, while acceptability refers to those strategies which are more likely to be put into action.

questions.text: In policy formulation, acceptability refers to:
options: Strategies that are valid and workable.
Strategies that are more likely to be put into action.
Strategies that are expensive to implement.
questions.answer: Strategies that are more likely to be put into action.
questions.explanation: Acceptability refers to those strategies which are more likely to be put into action. Effectiveness refers to valid, workable strategies.

questions.text: The process of making a rule or policy that is expected to have a binding effect on the populace is called:
questions.explanation: Rule making is the process of making a rule or policy that is expected to have a binding effect on the policy or the populace.

questions.text: The process by which rules are put to use for results to be gained is called:
questions.explanation: Rule implementation is the process by which rules, having been made, are put to use for results to be gained.

questions.text: The process by which a government reviews policy formulation and policy implementation and comes to a decision which determines successful formulation and implementation is called:
questions.explanation: Rule adjudication is the process by which a government reviews policy formulation and policy implementation and comes to a decision which determines successful formulation and implementation.

questions.text: Government as an academic field of study may be defined as:
options: The machinery established by the state to manage its affairs.
A body vested with power and authority for maintaining security.
The study of agencies, political institutions and the dynamics of the state.
A voluntary association of people with common interests.
questions.answer: The study of agencies, political institutions and the dynamics of the state.
questions.explanation: Government as an academic field of study may be defined as the study of agencies, political institutions and the dynamics of the state.

questions.text: As an academic field of study, government is regarded in most countries as a special subject studied in independent scholarly discipline labelled as all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Government as an academic field of study is labelled as 'government', 'political science', 'politics', or 'public affairs'. It is a social science subject, not a natural science.

questions.text: In Nigerian universities, the term most commonly used for the academic study of government is:
questions.explanation: In Nigerian universities, the term 'political science' is by far the most common, which is not a pure science but rather a social science subject.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a branch of government as an academic field of study?
questions.explanation: Astrophysics is not a branch of government. The academic branches of government include Public Administration, International Relations, Comparative Politics, Political Theory, Political Economy, and National Politics.

questions.text: The study of public administration focuses attention on:
options: The methods and techniques used by government functionaries in the management of state affairs.
questions.answer: The methods and techniques used by government functionaries in the management of state affairs.
questions.explanation: The study of public administration focuses attention on the methods and techniques used by government functionaries in the management of state affairs.

questions.text: Which branch of government as an academic field deals with relations between nations?
questions.explanation: International Relations deals with relations between nations as well as the environment within which these relations are maintained. It covers international organizations, international law, diplomacy, international economics, and foreign policy.

questions.text: The branch of government that focuses on the comparison of different governments in order to discover cross-cultural similarities and differences is:
questions.explanation: Comparative Politics focuses on the comparison of different governments in order to discover cross-cultural similarities and differences.

questions.text: The branch of government that concerns philosophical explanations related to the origin, form, behavior and purposes of human organisation is:
questions.explanation: Political Theory concerns philosophical explanations related to the origin, form, behavior and purposes of human organisation.

questions.text: The branch of government that deals with the fiscal and monetary policies of a country is:
questions.explanation: Political Economy deals with the fiscal and monetary policies of a country. It studies how politics influences economics and how economics affects politics.

questions.text: The branch of government that focuses on the organization of a specific government and teaches students about their own country is:
questions.explanation: National Politics focuses on the organization of a specific government. It teaches students about their own country under such topics as the legislature, the executive, the courts, the constitution, political parties, elections, and political awareness.

questions.text: Which of the following is a reason why government is an academic field of study?
options: It is being taught in schools, colleges and universities.
It has specialized areas in tertiary institutions.
It borrows ideas from other established disciplines.
questions.explanation: Government is an academic field of study because it is taught in schools, colleges and universities; it has specialized areas in tertiary institutions; it borrows ideas from other popular well-established disciplines; and it makes use of scientific methods, tools and statistics.

questions.text: Government as a school discipline borrows ideas from renowned philosophers like all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Government borrows ideas from renowned philosophers like Plato, Aristotle, Hobbes, Rousseau, John Locke, and Karl Marx. Albert Einstein was a physicist, not a political philosopher.

questions.text: In the study of government, public administration covers the:
options: Army, prison officers and public force.
Civil service, public corporations and local government.
Ministries of education, health and agriculture.
questions.answer: Ministries of education, health and agriculture.
questions.explanation: Public Administration in Government as a subject covers Education, Health Care and Agriculture. The study of Government in the field of public administration encourages knowledge on system of government, health care services and agriculture.

questions.text: Government as a subject refers to the study of:
options: The various nations of the world.
questions.explanation: Government can also be defined as the study of the constitution. The constitution is a guideline that helps the administrative structure and organs of government in carrying out their duties effectively without interference.

questions.text: Government can be defined as the study of:
questions.explanation: Government as an academic field of study involves the study of political institutions in the state. The political institution consists of political thinkers that help the people to rule themselves.

questions.text: The study of government in schools is important because the student can:
options: Be nominated for a trip abroad.
questions.explanation: The study of government in schools is important because the student can learn about their rights. It empowers learners with the knowledge of identifying their fundamental human rights as citizens.

questions.text: The structure of government implies the:
options: Organization of powers and functions of government.
Method of revenue allocation by government.
questions.answer: Organization of powers and functions of government.
questions.explanation: The structure of government implies the organization of powers and functions of government through the three organs of government.

questions.text: The study of government essentially facilitates the understanding of the:
options: Organization of the executive arm of government.
Functioning of the entire social formation.
questions.explanation: The study of government essentially facilitates the understanding of the governance of human societies and its ideology.

questions.text: Government as an academic field of study refers to the:
options: Study of political institutions and processes.
Working of the organs of government.
questions.answer: Study of political institutions and processes.
questions.explanation: Government as an academic field of study refers to the study of political institutions and its processes. It also educates us about different forms of government in the world.

questions.text: A common feature of government is:
questions.explanation: The common characteristic or attribute of government is the ability of making public policy.

questions.text: An indispensable feature of any government is:
questions.explanation: An indispensable feature of any government is political power.

questions.text: Government is different from other political organizations because:
options: It has legitimate power over citizens.
Its officials have fixed terms of office.
It can punish those who violate its rules.
It is made up of elected officials.
questions.answer: It has legitimate power over citizens.
questions.explanation: Government is different from other political organizations because government has legitimate power over its citizens.

questions.text: An ideology is essentially:
questions.explanation: An ideology is essentially a guide to political action. It is a set of opinions or beliefs of a group or an individual, often referring to a set of political beliefs.

questions.text: Which of the following defines the concept of government?
options: The process of administering justice in a country.
The process of supervising the activities of the legislature.
The orderly management and control of the affairs of a country.
The orderly transfer of power to duly elected politicians.
questions.answer: The orderly management and control of the affairs of a country.
questions.explanation: Government is defined as the orderly management and control of the affairs of a country.

questions.text: The institution and processes connected with making, enforcing and reviewing of laws in any society is referred to as:
questions.explanation: The institution and processes connected with making, enforcing and reviewing of laws in any society is referred to as government.

questions.text: Which of the following is a reason for studying government?
options: Knowledge of the rights of the individual.
Acquisition of skills to work in a state-owned establishment.
Helps the individual to form a pressure group.
Enables citizens to vote during election.
questions.answer: Knowledge of the rights of the individual.
questions.explanation: Government is a subject that empowers its learners with the ability/knowledge of identifying their fundamental human rights as citizens and how to defend themselves based on the constitution of the state.

questions.text: The study of Government offers an individual all the following EXCEPT:
options: Knowledge of his rights and duties.
Knowledge of the processes of government.
questions.explanation: Government as a subject empowers citizens with knowledge of their rights and obligations. It also trains them to become good citizens and enhances their knowledge of leadership and governance. It does not train someone to become a judge.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the subject matter of Government?
questions.explanation: Political power is an authority held by a group within a society that allows for the administration of public resources and implement policies for society.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a reason for studying government?
options: It helps to know the types of different systems of government in the world and how they operate.
It enhances people's knowledge about administration and other institutions involved in governance.
It guarantees automatic employment in government.
questions.answer: It guarantees automatic employment in government.
questions.explanation: The study of government does not guarantee automatic employment in government. However, it provides career opportunities in government, business, and international organizations.

questions.text: The study of government helps to prevent:
options: Mistakes of some past political leaders from being repeated.
questions.answer: Mistakes of some past political leaders from being repeated.
questions.explanation: The study of government helps to prevent mistakes of some past political leaders from being repeated.

questions.text: Government as a field of study promotes the spirit of:
options: Nationalism and patriotism in the lives of the people.
questions.answer: Nationalism and patriotism in the lives of the people.
questions.explanation: Government as a field of study promotes the spirit of nationalism and patriotism in the lives of the people.

questions.text: The study of government helps in opening the eyes of the people for the need to take part in:
options: Political decision making of a country.
questions.answer: Political decision making of a country.
questions.explanation: The study of government equally opens the eyes of the people for the need to take part in political decision making of a country.

questions.text: The study of government helps to develop the intellect because political analysis requires:
options: High degree of step-by-step logical approach.
questions.answer: High degree of step-by-step logical approach.
questions.explanation: The study of government helps to develop the intellect but it may be said that Government, perhaps, does it better than many other subjects because political analysis requires a high degree of step-by-step logical approach.

questions.text: Government makes the people know how conflict originates and:
questions.explanation: Government makes the people know how conflict originates and how it is resolved.

questions.text: The study of government helps the individual to understand the world he lives in. In fact, the student of Government is an encyclopedia on:
questions.explanation: The study of government helps the individual to understand the world he lives in. The student of Government is an encyclopedia on current affairs.

questions.text: Government grooms learners to become future:
questions.explanation: Government grooms the learners to become future political leaders.

bundles.name: Bundle 3 — The State: Definition, Features & Differences from Nation and Society

questions.text: A state may be defined as:
options: A politically organised body of people occupying a definite geographical territory, with an organised legitimate government.
A voluntary association of people with common interests.
A group of people who share the same language and culture.
A temporary organization that changes with every election.
questions.answer: A politically organised body of people occupying a definite geographical territory, with an organised legitimate government.
questions.explanation: A state may be defined as a politically organised body of people occupying a definite geographical territory, with an organised legitimate government.

questions.text: Which of the following is alternatively known as state?
questions.explanation: A state is alternatively known as a country. In most government textbooks, the term state refers to a country.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of a state?
questions.explanation: A state is a national or territory considered as an organized political community under one government. Maiduguri is a city, not a state. Examples of states include Nigeria, Ghana, Britain, USA, Senegal, and Canada.

questions.text: Which of the following is an essential feature of a state?
questions.explanation: An essential feature of a state is an organized system of laws. These laws are put in place to guide the members of the state.

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of a state?
questions.explanation: Territorial boundary is a feature of a state. A state has clear and well-defined boundaries separating it from other states.

questions.text: The most visible feature of a state is:
questions.explanation: The most visible feature of a state is its defined geographical territory. A state has clear and well-defined boundaries separating it from other states.

questions.text: The main attributes of a state are:
options: The press, the legislature, the executive and the judiciary.
Government, the police and the armed forces.
questions.explanation: The main attributes of a state are population, territory, government and sovereignty.

questions.text: The most distinguishing characteristic of the state is:
questions.explanation: The most distinguishing characteristic of the state is sovereignty. The supreme power to make decisions and enforce them on the people is with the state.

questions.text: Sovereignty is best defined as:
options: The absolute, supreme and ultimate dominion and authority of a political state.
The power of the government to make laws.
The ability of the state to defend its territory.
The recognition of the state by other states.
questions.answer: The absolute, supreme and ultimate dominion and authority of a political state.
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the absolute, supreme and ultimate dominion and authority of a political state, subject to no higher power expressed within its territory and in complete freedom from any outside influence.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a state?
questions.explanation: Temporary existence is not a feature of a state. The state is a permanent place that cannot be easily changed. Government may change but the state remains.

questions.text: The feature of a state that refers to the people who occupy it is:
questions.explanation: Population is an essential feature of a state because a state is occupied by people, and there is no limitation to the number of people making up a state in any constitution.

questions.text: The feature of a state that refers to its clear and well-defined boundaries is:
questions.explanation: Territory is the feature of a state that refers to its clear and well-defined boundaries separating it from other states, e.g., Nigeria and Cameroon or Benin Republic.

questions.text: The feature of a state that refers to its recognition both internally and externally is:
questions.explanation: Recognition is a feature of a state. A state must be recognised both internally and externally. The people of a state must realise and recognise the corporate existence of their state, while other states in the international environment must equally give recognition to an existing state.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about government as a feature of the state is CORRECT?
options: Government is a permanent feature of the state.
Government is not a permanent feature of the state but remains a significant feature.
Government and the state are the same.
Government is not necessary for a state.
questions.answer: Government is not a permanent feature of the state but remains a significant feature.
questions.explanation: Government is not a permanent feature of a state but it remains a significant feature because it is a machinery set up by the state to pilot the affairs of the people making up that state.

questions.text: The state is different from government because:
options: The state, unlike the government, is permanent.
The government is made up of powerful people.
Members of the government are elected.
The state can exercise absolute power.
questions.answer: The state, unlike the government, is permanent.
questions.explanation: The state is quite different from the government because the state is permanent; it has defined boundaries, armed forces, currency, etc. Government is tenured by election. It is temporary and must work based on the constitution of the state.

questions.text: A state is a special form of human association because it:
options: Has a legitimate monopoly of life and death penalties over its citizens.
Is the richest association in society.
Has a constitution approved by the citizens.
questions.answer: Has a legitimate monopoly of life and death penalties over its citizens.
questions.explanation: A state is a special form of human association because it has a legitimate monopoly of life and death penalties over its citizens.

questions.text: Which of the following groups has a compulsory membership?
questions.explanation: The state is a group of individuals that has compulsory membership. The members have no right to choose their state of origin.

questions.text: A state is different from other forms of human associations because membership is:
questions.explanation: A state is different from other forms of human associations because membership is obligatory (compulsory).

questions.text: A state may accommodate people of:
questions.explanation: A state may accommodate people from different states because a state can be defined as a territory with its own government and borders within a larger country.

questions.text: A society that is politically organized under a government is called a:
questions.explanation: A society that is politically organized under a government is called a sovereign state.

questions.text: The primary purpose of the state is to:
options: Establish a system of law and order.
Train people to become good citizens.
Cater for all the needs of the citizens.
Ensure the self-sufficiency of its people.
questions.answer: Establish a system of law and order.
questions.explanation: The establishment of law and order is the primary purpose of the state. A state without law and order is a place where everyone has the right to do whatsoever thing that he/she wishes.

questions.text: A state may be defined as a community of people:
options: With differing interests to control the government.
Organized as a unit for the purpose of government.
questions.explanation: A state may be defined as a politically organized body of people inhabiting a defined geographical entity with an organized legitimate government.

questions.text: A nation is best defined as a group of people with common:
questions.explanation: A nation is a stable community of people formed on the basis of a common language, territory, history, ethnicity or psychological makeup manifested in a common culture.

questions.text: A common language is one of the attributes of a:
questions.explanation: A nation could be seen as a body of people who feel themselves to be naturally linked together, share common ties, believe that they can live happily together. They share the same language, culture and have the feeling of nationality.

questions.text: A nation refers to a group of people who have similar:
questions.explanation: A nation has also been defined as a cultural-political community that has become conscious of its similar customs and traditions.

questions.text: A nation could be seen as a body of people who feel the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A nation is a body of people who feel they are naturally linked together, they live happily with each other, believe in one another and they see themselves as their brother's keeper.

questions.text: Which of the following is a difference between a state and a nation?
options: A state must be sovereign; people continue as a nation even if they do not remain sovereign.
A state is populated by homogeneous groups; a nation is populated by heterogeneous groups.
A state has racial connotation; a nation has no racial connotation.
A state is not recognized in international relations; a nation is recognized.
questions.answer: A state must be sovereign; people continue as a nation even if they do not remain sovereign.
questions.explanation: A state must be sovereign. People continue as a nation even if they do not remain sovereign. A state is populated by heterogeneous groups of people, while a nation is populated by homogeneous groups of people.

questions.text: A state is populated by:
options: People of the same language only.
People of the same culture only.
questions.explanation: A state is populated by heterogeneous groups of people. A nation is populated by homogeneous groups of people.

questions.text: A nation is populated by:
questions.explanation: A nation is populated by homogeneous groups of people. A state is populated by heterogeneous groups of people.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about a nation is CORRECT?
options: A nation is recognized as an actor in international relations.
A nation can enter into agreements or treaties with states at the international level.
A nation has racial significance and is limited to a particular geographical entity.
A nation has no common ties among its people.
questions.answer: A nation has racial significance and is limited to a particular geographical entity.
questions.explanation: A nation has racial significance. It is limited to a particular geographical entity and has its own peculiar features. A state, not a nation, is recognized as an actor in international relations.

questions.text: Nationalism is best defined as:
options: The sense of belonging and love for a nation as a result of shared attributes.
The desire to create a new state.
The feeling of superiority over other nations.
questions.answer: The sense of belonging and love for a nation as a result of shared attributes.
questions.explanation: Nationalism is the sense of belonging and love for a nation as a result of shared attributes, namely: race, language, geographical location, religion and political aspirations.

questions.text: The spirit of nationalism can manifest in institutions like:
questions.explanation: The spirit of Nationalism can manifest in institutions like state and nation.

questions.text: A society is best defined as:
options: A group of individuals involved in persistent social interaction, sharing the same spatial or social territory.
A politically organized body of people with a government.
A group of people with a common language and culture.
A temporary association of people with common interests.
questions.answer: A group of individuals involved in persistent social interaction, sharing the same spatial or social territory.
questions.explanation: A society is a group of individuals involved in persistent social interaction, or a large social group sharing the same spatial or social territory, typically subject to the same political authority and dominant cultural expectations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of a society?
options: It has a defined geographical territory.
questions.explanation: Membership of a society is voluntary. A state has compulsory membership.

questions.text: A society is ______ in nature.
questions.explanation: A society is permanent in nature. It is characterised by unique culture and common history, tradition, language, religion and sense of values.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a society?
options: It is controlled by rules, regulations, norms, conventions and customs.
It applies sanctions on its members as a means of ensuring discipline.
questions.explanation: Membership of a society is voluntary, not compulsory. Membership of a state is compulsory.

questions.text: The difference between the state and society is that:
options: The state has no fixed territory; society has a fixed territory.
The state has the power to enforce laws; society has no power to enforce laws.
The state has no sovereignty; society has sovereignty.
The state came into existence before society.
questions.answer: The state has the power to enforce laws; society has no power to enforce laws.
questions.explanation: The state has the power to enforce laws, while society has no power to enforce laws. The state has a fixed territory, while society has no fixed territory.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the state and society is CORRECT?
options: The scope of the state is wider than that of society.
The scope of society is wider than that of the state.
The state and society have the same scope.
Society has sovereignty while the state does not.
questions.answer: The scope of society is wider than that of the state.
questions.explanation: The scope of society is much wider than that of the state. The state indicates a political system, while society is a broader social system.

questions.text: Which of the following is a basic function of a state?
questions.explanation: The basic functions of a state include defensive function, administrative function, international relations, provision of social security, and economic functions.

questions.text: The function of the state that includes defence from external aggression and maintenance of law and order is:
questions.explanation: The defensive function of the state includes defence from external aggression and maintenance of law and order, as these two are essential for economic development.

questions.text: The function of the state that involves setting up administrative structures and agencies for administering and controlling different departments is:
questions.explanation: The administrative function of the state involves setting up administrative structures and agencies for administering and controlling the different departments in the country.

questions.text: The function of the state that involves maintaining friendly relations with other states in the world is:
questions.explanation: The international relations function of the state involves maintaining friendly relations with other states in the world, including participation in international organizations, conferences, and joint treaties.

questions.text: The function of the state that includes insurance against accident, assistance to the poor, the sick and the unemployed is:
questions.explanation: The provision of social security function includes insurance against accident, assistance to the poor, the sick and the unemployed, and the promotion of natural and human resources.

questions.text: Which of the following is an economic function of the state?
options: Assessing, exploring and making optimum utilization of natural resources.
Ensuring growth by maintaining economic stability.
Reduction of economic disparities by minimizing the gap between rich and poor.
questions.explanation: Economic functions of the state include assessing, exploring and making optimum utilization of natural resources; ensuring growth by maintaining economic stability; reduction of economic disparities; and increasing economic growth.

questions.text: The state must protect its citizens from outside attack while also ensuring domestic peace. This is the function of:
questions.explanation: The establishment of order function requires the state to protect its citizens from outside attack while also ensuring domestic peace.

questions.text: The state must provide conditions necessary for the full development of every citizen, including the protection of individual liberty. This is the function of:
questions.explanation: The promotion of individual's welfare function requires the state to provide conditions necessary for the full development of every citizen, including the protection of individual liberty.

questions.text: The state must strive to ensure happiness for the greatest number of citizens living within the state. This is the function of:
questions.explanation: The promotion of general welfare function requires the state to strive to ensure happiness for the greatest number of citizens living within the state.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a difference between a state and other human associations?
options: Membership of a state is compulsory; membership of other associations is voluntary.
Rules made by the state are binding on all residents; rules of other associations are not applicable to non-members.
The state has legitimate authority to punish law breakers; other associations do not.
The state is a temporary association; other associations are permanent.
questions.answer: The state is a temporary association; other associations are permanent.
questions.explanation: The state is a permanent association, while other associations are non-permanent and may disappear and re-emerge. Therefore, the statement that the state is temporary is incorrect.

questions.text: The state can use force to ensure that its citizens obey its laws and regulations. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: The state can use force to ensure that its citizens obey its laws and regulations. This is an example of the coercive power of the state.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct statement about the relationship between the state and government?
options: The state is temporary while the government is permanent.
The state is permanent while the government is temporary.
The state and government are the same.
The government is more inclusive than the state.
questions.answer: The state is permanent while the government is temporary.
questions.explanation: The state is permanent while the government is temporary. Government may change but the state remains. The state is more inclusive and greater than government.

bundles.name: Bundle 4 — Functions of Government & Importance of Studying Government

questions.text: Which of the following is the primary function of government in a state?
questions.explanation: The primary function of any government is to maintain peace, law and order in society before the government can function properly.

questions.text: The functions of government include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Protection of citizens from malicious attack.
questions.explanation: It is the responsibility of the government to make provision for maintenance of peace and order, social services, and basic amenities and infrastructure. The government provides health centres and hospitals, but not necessarily free medical services for all.

questions.text: The state performs the following functions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Government can never encourage the struggle for power; it encourages peace and unity in society. The struggle for power can lead to riots and demonstrations that disturb the peace and order of society.

questions.text: Government can be made responsible and accountable to its citizens through the following methods EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Government can be responsible and accountable to its citizens through periodic change of government, political education, and public opinion. Demonstration is a form of violence, not a formal process of deliberations.

questions.text: The functions of the state are achieved through:
questions.explanation: The three organs of government are the administrative order of government. The executive formulates and implements policies, the legislature makes laws, and the judiciary interprets the laws.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable function of government?
questions.explanation: Subversion is not an acceptable function of the government. Subversion means the act of trying to destroy or damage an established system or government.

questions.text: A government performs the following functions EXCEPT:
options: Providing all the needs of its citizens.
questions.answer: Providing all the needs of its citizens.
questions.explanation: It is impossible for the government to provide all the needs of its citizens. The government safeguards lives and property, maintains laws and orders, and provides basic welfare needs.

questions.text: The defense of a country is a major function of the:
questions.explanation: The government has the function of defending the state from external and internal aggression. It is the duty of the armed forces of a country to maintain the territorial integrity of the state.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a duty of government?
options: To defend and protect the lives and properties of its citizens.
To provide and enhance employment opportunities.
To encourage citizens to take the law into their own hands.
questions.answer: To encourage citizens to take the law into their own hands.
questions.explanation: Government does not encourage citizens to take the law into their own hands. It administers justice through the settlement of disputes by the judiciary.

questions.text: Which of the following is a duty of government?
options: To protect the fundamental human rights of citizens.
To maintain external relationships with other countries.
To promote and protect national interest.
questions.explanation: The duties of government include maintaining law and order, defending and protecting lives and property, providing employment opportunities, administering justice, protecting fundamental human rights, maintaining external relationships, and promoting national interest.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of government?
questions.explanation: Government can never encourage the struggle for power. It encourages peace and unity in society.

questions.text: The function of government that involves maintaining good relationships with other countries is:
questions.explanation: The external affairs function of government involves maintaining good relationships with other countries through embassies, high commissions, ambassadors, and high commissioners.

questions.text: The function of government that involves the judiciary is:
questions.explanation: The judiciary is responsible for the administration of justice in the state.

questions.text: Which of the following is a source of government revenue?
questions.explanation: Sources of government revenue include tax, surplus of public sector units, fines and penalties, gifts and grants, borrowings, rates, and fees.

questions.text: The promotion of economic function of government includes:
options: Regulating economic activities to protect the economy.
Ensuring economic growth and development through careful economic planning.
questions.explanation: Government has the responsibility of regulating economic activities in order to protect the economy and ensure economic growth and development through careful economic planning and execution.

questions.text: The provision of employment is a function of government because:
options: It is the duty of the government to provide employment opportunities to its citizens.
Some countries pay unemployment allowance to citizens whom the government failed to provide gainful employment.
Government is the largest employer of labour.
questions.explanation: It is the duty of the government to provide employment opportunities to its citizens. This is one of the reasons why some countries pay unemployment allowance to citizens whom the government failed to provide gainful employment.

questions.text: Formulation and implementation of policies are carried out by the:
questions.explanation: Formulation and implementation of policies are carried out to ensure the well-being of the people. The executive arm of government performs this function.

questions.text: Administration of justice is the responsibility of the:
questions.explanation: The judiciary is responsible for the administration of justice in the state.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of government?
options: Provision of social amenities and basic infrastructure.
questions.explanation: Government does not encourage civil disobedience. It maintains law and order, provides social amenities, and promotes economic function.

questions.text: The function of government that involves the provision of portable water, health centres, electricity, housing, hospitals, good roads, and markets is:
options: Provision of social amenities and basic infrastructure.
questions.answer: Provision of social amenities and basic infrastructure.
questions.explanation: The provision of social amenities and basic infrastructure includes portable water, health centres, electricity, housing, hospitals, good roads, and markets.

questions.text: Which of the following is a reason for studying government?
questions.explanation: Reasons for studying government include objective reasoning, intellectual development, understanding types of systems, widening people's knowledge, development of good political culture, decision making, conflict resolution, improvement of social consciousness, opportunity for leadership, career opportunities, and rights knowing.

questions.text: The study of government enables us to reason objectively because it teaches us how to:
options: Analyse critically the political, social and economic events within and outside our immediate environment.
questions.answer: Analyse critically the political, social and economic events within and outside our immediate environment.
questions.explanation: The study of government as a discipline enables us to reason objectively. It teaches us how to analyse critically the political, social and economic events within and outside our immediate environment.

questions.text: Citizens with sound knowledge of government would be in good positions to understand the:
options: Types of system of government adopted in their country and the implications of such systems.
questions.answer: Types of system of government adopted in their country and the implications of such systems.
questions.explanation: Citizens with sound knowledge of government would be in good positions to understand the types of system of government adopted in their country and the implications of such systems of government.

questions.text: The study of government helps to widen people's knowledge about:
options: Administration and other institutions involved in governance.
questions.answer: Administration and other institutions involved in governance.
questions.explanation: The study of government helps to widen people's knowledge about administration and other institutions involved in governance.

questions.text: Through the study of government, the people develop:
questions.explanation: Through the study of government, the people develop positive political culture. They will be able to acquire some values that help them contribute meaningfully in the development of society.

questions.text: The study of government opens the eyes of the people for the need to take part in:
options: Political decision making of a country.
questions.answer: Political decision making of a country.
questions.explanation: The study of government equally opens the eyes of the people for the need to take part in political decision making of a country.

questions.text: The study of government helps to develop the intellect because political analysis requires:
options: High degree of step-by-step logical approach.
questions.answer: High degree of step-by-step logical approach.
questions.explanation: The study of government helps to develop the intellect but it may be said that Government, perhaps, does it better than many other subjects because political analysis requires a high degree of step-by-step logical approach.

questions.text: Government makes the people know how conflict originates and:
questions.explanation: Government makes the people know how conflict originates and how it is resolved.

questions.text: The study of government helps the individual to understand the world he lives in. In fact, the student of Government is an encyclopedia on:
questions.explanation: The study of government helps the individual to understand the world he lives in. The student of Government is an encyclopedia on current affairs.

questions.text: Government grooms learners to become future:
questions.explanation: Government grooms the learners to become future political leaders.

questions.text: The study of government provides career opportunities to people in:
questions.explanation: The study of government provides career opportunities to people. Candidates with degrees in government or political science are in high demand in government, business, international organizations, etc.

questions.text: Government provides the opportunity to make its citizens know their:
questions.explanation: Government provides the opportunity to make its citizens know their rights, duties and obligations.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a reason for studying government?
options: It helps to know the types of different systems of government in the world and how they operate.
It enhances people's knowledge about administration and other institutions involved in governance.
It guarantees automatic employment in government.
questions.answer: It guarantees automatic employment in government.
questions.explanation: The study of government does not guarantee automatic employment in government. However, it provides career opportunities in government, business, and international organizations.

questions.text: The study of government helps to prevent:
options: Mistakes of some past political leaders from being repeated.
questions.answer: Mistakes of some past political leaders from being repeated.
questions.explanation: The study of government helps to prevent mistakes of some past political leaders from being repeated.

questions.text: Government as a field of study promotes the spirit of:
options: Nationalism and patriotism in the lives of the people.
questions.answer: Nationalism and patriotism in the lives of the people.
questions.explanation: Government as a field of study promotes the spirit of nationalism and patriotism in the lives of the people.

questions.text: The study of government essentially facilitates the understanding of the:
options: Organization of the executive arm of government.
Functioning of the entire social formation.
questions.explanation: The study of government essentially facilitates the understanding of the governance of human societies and its ideology.

questions.text: Which of the following is a function of government?
questions.explanation: Functions of government include law making, protection of lives and property, defence of the country, maintenance of law and order, provision of social amenities, provision of employment, promotion of economic function, formulation and implementation of policies, administration of justice, and external affairs function.

questions.text: Government maintains law and order through the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Government makes laws and enforces them on the people through the legislature, police and prison services. Immigration is not primarily a law and order maintenance organ in this context.

questions.text: Which of the following is a means by which government maintains law and order?
options: Maintenance of police and other security personnel.
questions.answer: Maintenance of police and other security personnel.
questions.explanation: Government maintains law and order through law making, maintenance of police and other security personnel, and effective communication network. Establishment of professional associations is not a means by which government maintains law and order.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a means by which government maintains law and order?
options: Maintenance of police and other security personnel.
questions.explanation: Establishment of professional associations is not a means by which government maintains law and order.

questions.explanation: It is impossible for the government to provide all the needs of its citizens. The government safeguards lives and property, maintains laws and orders, and provides basic welfare needs.

To promote and protect national interest.
